name: CTET Paper 1
fullName: Central Teacher Eligibility Test – Paper I (Primary Stage, Classes I–V)
frequency: Usually twice a year (sessions are sometimes skipped or shifted)
approxCandidates: ≈10.65 lakh appeared for Paper 1 in the Feb 2026 session (Papers 1 + 2 together: 26.5 lakh registered, 23.2 lakh appeared)
eligibility: Senior Secondary (50%) plus a 2-year D.El.Ed or 4-year B.El.Ed (final-year students may apply), or an equivalent qualification under NCTE norms. No upper age limit, and the certificate is valid for life.

notification.summary: The September 2026 (22nd) CTET was notified by CBSE around 11 May 2026 and scheduled in offline OMR mode on 6 Sep 2026. Applications are closed and the result is awaited. The previous (Feb 2026) result was declared on 30–31 Mar 2026 with a 33.69% pass rate in Paper 1. The next cycle's notification is expected around Nov–Dec 2026. Dates come from news reports found by web search on 2026-10-10, because ctet.nic.in could not be reached from the research sandbox. Verify on the official site.
notification.source: https://ctet.nic.in (official), cross-checked with the CBSE Feb 2026 result notice https://www.cbse.gov.in/cbsenew/documents/PUBLIC_%20NOTICE_CTET_Feb_2026_RESULT_31032026.pdf and Careers360/PW news reports

pattern.notes: Real paper: 150 MCQs of 1 mark each, no negative marking, 2½ hours. Qualifying marks are 60% (90/150) for General and 55% (82/150) for SC/ST/OBC/PwD. Candidates choose Language I and Language II from 20 languages, and they must be different. This mock uses English as Language I and Hindi as Language II. The question bank holds 60 original questions (12 per section), so a mock built from it is a scaled-down version of the full 150-question paper. About half of each Maths, EVS and Language section is pedagogy.

trendAnalysis.summary: This analysis covers the Jul 2024, Dec 2024 and Feb 2026 sessions. No CTET exam was held in calendar 2025: the Dec-2025 cycle was conducted on 8 Feb 2026. Overall difficulty is easy to moderate. CDP and the pedagogy halves of Maths and EVS decide the score, and they increasingly use classroom-scenario and NCF-2005/NEP-2020 based questions rather than definitions. Inclusive education (RPwD Act, learning disabilities), assessment for learning, and Piaget/Vygotsky applications are high-yield in CDP. Maths content stays at primary level (place value, fractions, time, measurement, patterns, data), while pedagogy focuses on error analysis and Van Hiele levels. EVS content is drawn from NCERT Looking Around (Classes III–V) themes such as animals, water, shelter and travel. The Feb 2026 Paper 1 pass rate was 33.69%.

resources.notes: CBSE does not keep a public archive of CTET question papers. After each exam it posts the provisional answer key together with each candidate's scanned OMR sheet and question-paper set under 'Candidate Activity' on ctet.nic.in for a short challenge window. Final keys and result notices are published on ctet.nic.in and cbse.gov.in. Full past papers in circulation are reconstructions by coaching publishers, not official copies.

questions.question: A four-year-old insists that the moon follows her when she walks because it wants to play with her. According to Piaget, this belief is an example of:
questions.explanation: In Piaget's pre-operational stage (2–7 years), children believe that lifeless objects have life, feelings and intentions. This is called animism.

relevance.note: Classic CTET 'moon follows me' animism scenario; distractors are other Piagetian terms

questions.question: A child says, "I will not take my friend's eraser without asking because the teacher will punish me." According to Kohlberg, the child's reasoning reflects the:
questions.explanation: The child judges the action by its consequence (punishment). This is Stage 1 of Kohlberg's pre-conventional level.

relevance.note: Faithful Kohlberg statement-to-stage item as set in CTET; fear of punishment cue is standard

questions.question: A baby gains control over the head and neck before gaining control over the legs. This illustrates the:
questions.explanation: Development proceeds from head to tail (cephalocaudal). The proximodistal principle describes development from the centre of the body outward.

relevance.note: Head-before-legs cephalocaudal is a staple CTET development-principle item; proximodistal is the right trap

questions.question: According to Howard Gardner, a child who easily understands the feelings of classmates and works well in groups shows strength in which intelligence?
questions.explanation: Interpersonal intelligence is the ability to understand and interact effectively with others. Intrapersonal intelligence concerns understanding oneself.

relevance.note: Gardner profile-to-intelligence as in CTET; intrapersonal is the expected trap

questions.question: A teacher always asks girls to sweep the classroom and boys to carry the benches. This practice reflects:
questions.explanation: Assigning tasks according to fixed notions of what boys and girls should do reinforces gender stereotypes.

relevance.note: Chore allocation by gender -> stereotyping is a recurring CTET scenario

questions.question: The main purpose of 'assessment for learning' is to:
options: Give ongoing feedback that helps improve teaching and learning
Compare the performance of different schools
Certify students for promotion to the next class
Rank students at the end of the year
questions.explanation: Assessment for learning (formative assessment) happens during instruction and uses feedback to improve learning. Ranking and certification are summative purposes.

relevance.note: Assessment for learning purpose is asked almost every CTET cycle; distractors are summative uses

questions.topic: Inclusive Education & Children with Special Needs
questions.question: A child of average intelligence has persistent difficulty in decoding words, reverses letters while reading and reads very slowly. The child most likely has:
questions.explanation: Dyslexia is a specific learning disability that affects reading and word decoding. Dyscalculia affects number skills, dysgraphia affects writing, and dyspraxia affects motor coordination.

relevance.note: Letter reversal/decoding -> dyslexia, exact CTET symptom-to-disorder pattern

questions.question: From a constructivist point of view, the errors children make while learning are best seen as:
options: Unimportant details that the teacher should ignore
Signs of carelessness that must be penalised
Windows into children's thinking that help the teacher plan instruction
questions.explanation: Errors reveal children's reasoning and misconceptions, so teachers use them diagnostically.

relevance.note: 'Errors as windows into thinking' is one of the most repeated CTET CDP ideas

questions.question:
Read the passage and answer.

"Every monsoon, the village of Kalpur faced the same problem: the only road to the school turned into a stream of mud, and children often missed classes for weeks. In 2019, a group of parents decided they would not wait any longer. Using stones from a nearby quarry and labour donated on weekends, they built a raised footpath along the edge of the fields. The work took four months. Today, attendance during the rainy season is almost as high as in any other season, and the footpath is maintained by the students themselves, who take turns clearing it every Saturday."

Why did children often miss classes in Kalpur?
options: The quarry blocked the road to the school
The road to school turned into mud during the monsoon
Parents needed them to work in the fields
The school was closed during the rainy season
questions.explanation: The passage says the only road to school 'turned into a stream of mud' every monsoon, so children missed classes.

relevance.note: Factual detail from short prose passage; matches CTET Language I comprehension

Who looks after the footpath today?
options: The students, who take turns clearing it
questions.explanation: The last sentence says the footpath is maintained by the students, who take turns clearing it every Saturday.

relevance.note: Direct retrieval from passage; distractors reuse passage nouns as in CTET

questions.question:
Read the passage and answer.

"Every monsoon, the village of Kalpur faced the same problem: the only road to the school turned into a stream of mud, and children often missed classes for weeks. In 2019, a group of parents decided they would not wait any longer. Using stones from a nearby quarry and labour donated on weekends, they built a raised footpath along the edge of the fields. The work took four months. Today, attendance during the rainy season is almost as high as in any other season, and the footpath is maintained by the students themselves, who take turns clearing it every Saturday."

The word 'donated' in the passage is closest in meaning to:
questions.explanation: To donate is to give something without payment. The parents gave their weekend labour free of cost.

relevance.note: Word-in-context meaning item typical of CTET passages

questions.question:
Read the passage and answer.

"Every monsoon, the village of Kalpur faced the same problem: the only road to the school turned into a stream of mud, and children often missed classes for weeks. In 2019, a group of parents decided they would not wait any longer. Using stones from a nearby quarry and labour donated on weekends, they built a raised footpath along the edge of the fields. The work took four months. Today, attendance during the rainy season is almost as high as in any other season, and the footpath is maintained by the students themselves, who take turns clearing it every Saturday."

In the phrase 'a raised footpath', the word 'raised' is used as:
questions.explanation: 'Raised' (a past participle) describes the noun 'footpath', so here it functions as an adjective.

relevance.note: Participle-as-adjective from passage; CTET grammar-from-passage format

questions.question:
Read the stanza and answer.

"The old banyan by the river stands,
It holds the evening in its hands;
The birds come home, the shadows creep,
And all the village falls asleep."

The line 'It holds the evening in its hands' contains which poetic device?
questions.explanation: The banyan tree is given a human action (holding something in its hands). This is personification.

relevance.note: Personification in a poem line matches CTET poem-based items

questions.question:
Read the stanza and answer.

"The old banyan by the river stands,
It holds the evening in its hands;
The birds come home, the shadows creep,
And all the village falls asleep."

The rhyme scheme of the stanza is:
questions.explanation: stands/hands rhyme (a, a) and creep/asleep rhyme (b, b), so the scheme is aabb.

relevance.note: Rhyme scheme stands/hands, creep/asleep = aabb; CTET poem item

questions.question: According to Stephen Krashen, children acquire a language most effectively when they:
options: Are corrected immediately for every error
Receive plenty of comprehensible input in a low-anxiety environment
Translate every sentence into their mother tongue
Memorise grammar rules before using the language
questions.explanation: Krashen's Input Hypothesis and Affective Filter Hypothesis say that acquisition happens through comprehensible input when anxiety is low.

relevance.note: Krashen comprehensible input/affective filter is a regular CTET pedagogy item

questions.question: Which is the most appropriate way to assess the speaking skills of Class 4 learners?
options: A role-play or show-and-tell assessed with a simple rubric
questions.explanation: Speaking is assessed through actual oral performance. Role-play or show-and-tell, judged against criteria such as fluency and clarity, does this.

relevance.note: Role play with rubric for speaking assessment, CTET-style assessment item

questions.question: The 'whole language' approach to teaching English in the primary classes emphasises:
options: Learning language through meaningful, authentic texts and contexts
Drilling isolated letters and sounds before any reading
Translating texts word by word into the mother tongue
Memorising lists of words and their spellings
questions.explanation: The whole language approach treats language as a whole system of meaning and uses real stories, conversations and texts instead of fragmented drills.

relevance.note: Whole-language approach definition as asked in CTET English pedagogy

questions.question: Which activity best develops the listening skill of Class 3 learners?
options: Writing the spellings of difficult words
Listening to a story and then arranging picture cards in the order of events
questions.explanation: Sequencing pictures after listening requires children to attend to and understand spoken input, so it builds listening comprehension.

relevance.note: Listening activity choice with plausible distractors; CTET-like

questions.question:
गद्यांश पढ़कर प्रश्न का उत्तर दीजिए।

"पानी हमारे जीवन का आधार है। धरती पर उपलब्ध कुल जल का बहुत छोटा भाग ही पीने योग्य है। बढ़ती जनसंख्या और लापरवाही के कारण यह सीमित भंडार तेज़ी से घट रहा है। यदि हम वर्षा के जल का संचयन करें, नलों को खुला न छोड़ें और नदियों को प्रदूषित होने से बचाएँ, तो आने वाली पीढ़ियों के लिए भी पर्याप्त जल बचा रहेगा।"

गद्यांश के अनुसार पीने योग्य जल का भंडार घटने का मुख्य कारण क्या है?
questions.explanation: गद्यांश में स्पष्ट लिखा है कि 'बढ़ती जनसंख्या और लापरवाही के कारण' सीमित भंडार घट रहा है।

relevance.note: गद्यांश से कारण पूछना — CTET हिंदी भाषा-I का मानक प्रश्न

questions.question:
गद्यांश पढ़कर प्रश्न का उत्तर दीजिए।

"पानी हमारे जीवन का आधार है। धरती पर उपलब्ध कुल जल का बहुत छोटा भाग ही पीने योग्य है। बढ़ती जनसंख्या और लापरवाही के कारण यह सीमित भंडार तेज़ी से घट रहा है। यदि हम वर्षा के जल का संचयन करें, नलों को खुला न छोड़ें और नदियों को प्रदूषित होने से बचाएँ, तो आने वाली पीढ़ियों के लिए भी पर्याप्त जल बचा रहेगा।"

'संचयन' शब्द का अर्थ है —
questions.explanation: संचयन का अर्थ है एकत्र या इकट्ठा करना। वर्षा जल संचयन = वर्षा का पानी इकट्ठा करना।

relevance.note: गद्यांश के शब्द का अर्थ — CTET प्रारूप

questions.question:
गद्यांश पढ़कर प्रश्न का उत्तर दीजिए।

"पानी हमारे जीवन का आधार है। धरती पर उपलब्ध कुल जल का बहुत छोटा भाग ही पीने योग्य है। बढ़ती जनसंख्या और लापरवाही के कारण यह सीमित भंडार तेज़ी से घट रहा है। यदि हम वर्षा के जल का संचयन करें, नलों को खुला न छोड़ें और नदियों को प्रदूषित होने से बचाएँ, तो आने वाली पीढ़ियों के लिए भी पर्याप्त जल बचा रहेगा।"

'जनसंख्या' शब्द में कौन-सा समास है?
questions.explanation: जनसंख्या = जन की संख्या। यहाँ 'की' (संबंध) विभक्ति का लोप है, अतः यह षष्ठी तत्पुरुष समास है।

relevance.note: जन की संख्या = षष्ठी तत्पुरुष; गद्यांश-शब्द पर समास प्रश्न CTET में आता है

questions.question:
गद्यांश पढ़कर प्रश्न का उत्तर दीजिए।

"पानी हमारे जीवन का आधार है। धरती पर उपलब्ध कुल जल का बहुत छोटा भाग ही पीने योग्य है। बढ़ती जनसंख्या और लापरवाही के कारण यह सीमित भंडार तेज़ी से घट रहा है। यदि हम वर्षा के जल का संचयन करें, नलों को खुला न छोड़ें और नदियों को प्रदूषित होने से बचाएँ, तो आने वाली पीढ़ियों के लिए भी पर्याप्त जल बचा रहेगा।"

गद्यांश के लिए सबसे उपयुक्त शीर्षक है —
questions.explanation: पूरा गद्यांश जल के महत्व और उसे बचाने के उपायों पर केंद्रित है, अतः 'जल संरक्षण' उपयुक्त शीर्षक है।

relevance.note: उपयुक्त शीर्षक — CTET गद्यांश प्रश्न

questions.question: प्राथमिक कक्षाओं में पढ़ने की रुचि और कौशल विकसित करने के लिए सबसे उपयुक्त उपाय है —
options: बच्चों को उनकी रुचि की कहानियाँ और बाल-साहित्य उपलब्ध कराना
questions.explanation: सार्थक और रोचक बाल-साहित्य से बच्चे पढ़ने का आनंद लेते हैं और अर्थ ग्रहण करते हुए पढ़ना सीखते हैं।

relevance.note: बाल-साहित्य से पठन-रुचि — CTET pedagogy item, distractors somewhat weak

questions.question: कक्षा 3 के बच्चों की मौखिक अभिव्यक्ति का आकलन करने का सबसे उपयुक्त तरीका है —
options: किसी अनुभव या चित्र पर बच्चों से बातचीत करवाना
questions.explanation: मौखिक अभिव्यक्ति का आकलन बोलने के अवसर देकर ही हो सकता है, जैसे अनुभव सुनाना या चित्र पर बातचीत करना।

relevance.note: मौखिक अभिव्यक्ति आकलन via बातचीत — CTET assessment item

questions.question: विद्यालय आने से पहले अधिकांश बच्चे —
options: अपनी घर की भाषा में सार्थक संवाद करने की क्षमता लेकर आते हैं
भाषा से पूरी तरह अनजान होते हैं
व्याकरण के सभी नियम जानते हैं
questions.explanation: बच्चे परिवेश से भाषा अर्जित कर लेते हैं और विद्यालय आने तक अपनी भाषा में सहज संवाद कर पाते हैं।

relevance.note: Children bring home-language competence to school — repeated CTET statement

questions.question: What is the difference between the place value and the face value of 7 in the number 47,215?
questions.explanation: Place value of 7 = 7000 and face value = 7. Difference = 7000 − 7 = 6993.

relevance.note: Place value minus face value 7000-7=6993 with 0/7007 traps; CTET maths classic

questions.question: Which of the following fractions is the greatest: 3/4, 5/8, 2/3, 7/12?

relevance.note: Fraction comparison; in-syllabus but plain computation rather than CTET's misconception framing

questions.question: A train leaves a station at 10:45 a.m. and reaches its destination at 2:20 p.m. on the same day. How long is the journey?
questions.explanation: 10:45 a.m. → 1:45 p.m. is 3 h, and 1:45 p.m. → 2:20 p.m. is 35 min. Total = 3 h 35 min.

relevance.note: a.m.-p.m. elapsed time 3h35m with 4h35 trap; CTET maths type

questions.question: A rectangular garden is 12 m long and 8 m wide. How much wire is needed to fence it with 3 rounds of wire?
questions.explanation: Perimeter = 2(12 + 8) = 40 m. For 3 rounds, 3 × 40 = 120 m.

relevance.note: Fencing with rounds, area 96 as trap; faithful CTET mensuration

questions.question: What comes next in the pattern 2, 5, 10, 17, 26, …?
questions.explanation: The differences are 3, 5, 7, 9, so the next difference is 11 and 26 + 11 = 37. (Equivalently, the terms are n² + 1.)

relevance.note: Odd-difference series 2,5,10,17,26 -> 37; CTET pattern item

questions.question: Add: 3 kg 250 g + 1 kg 875 g = ?
questions.explanation: 250 g + 875 g = 1125 g = 1 kg 125 g. Then 3 kg + 1 kg + 1 kg = 5 kg. Total = 5 kg 125 g.

relevance.note: kg-g addition with carry 5 kg 125 g; distractors from carry errors as in CTET

questions.question: In a pictograph, one symbol stands for 4 students. Class A is shown by 6½ symbols and Class B by 4 symbols. How many more students are in Class A than in Class B?
questions.explanation: Class A = 6.5 × 4 = 26 and Class B = 4 × 4 = 16. Difference = 10.

relevance.note: Pictograph with half symbol and scale 4 -> 10; faithful CTET data-handling item

questions.topic: Place of Maths in Curriculum & Language of Maths
questions.question: According to NCF 2005, the main goal of mathematics education in school is:
options: Mathematisation of the child's thought processes
questions.explanation: NCF 2005 states that the main goal is the mathematisation of the child's thinking, that is, developing the ability to think and reason mathematically.

relevance.note: NCF 2005 'mathematisation' goal is asked repeatedly in CTET maths pedagogy

questions.question: A child writes 46 − 28 = 22. What is the most likely reason for the error?
options: The child has not memorised multiplication tables
The child copied the numbers incorrectly
In each column the child subtracts the smaller digit from the larger one instead of regrouping
The child added the numbers instead of subtracting them
questions.explanation: The child computed 8 − 6 = 2 in the ones column and 4 − 2 = 2 in the tens column. This is the classic 'smaller-from-larger' error: the child did not regroup. The correct answer is 18. Adding would give 74.

relevance.note: Smaller-from-larger subtraction bug 46-28=22; exactly CTET error-analysis format

questions.question: Which task best assesses a Class 4 child's conceptual understanding of fractions?
options: Shade 3/4 of a figure in two different ways and explain why both are correct
Recite that a fraction is 'numerator over denominator'
Write the definition of a fraction
Copy the fractions written on the blackboard
questions.explanation: Representing a fraction in more than one way and justifying it shows understanding, not just recall.

relevance.note: Conceptual-understanding task choice; correct option stands out but CTET-faithful

questions.question: A child identifies a figure as a 'square' because 'it looks like a window', but cannot describe any of its properties. According to the van Hiele model, the child is at the level of:
questions.explanation: At van Hiele Level 0 (visualisation), shapes are recognised by their overall appearance and not by their properties. Properties are noticed at Level 1 (analysis).

relevance.note: van Hiele visualisation from 'looks like a window' reasoning; CTET favourite

questions.topic: Family & Friends (relationships, animals, plants, work & play)
questions.question: Which bird stitches the edges of leaves together with plant fibre to make its nest?
questions.explanation: The tailorbird punctures leaf edges and stitches them together to form a cup-shaped nest. The weaver bird weaves grass strips, the crow piles up twigs, and the koel lays its eggs in a crow's nest.

relevance.note: Tailorbird stitching from NCERT EVS; weaver bird is the right trap

questions.question: 'Tanka' (or 'kund'), an underground tank used to collect rainwater for drinking, is a traditional water-harvesting structure mainly found in:
questions.explanation: Tankas and kunds are typical of arid Rajasthan. Meghalaya is known for bamboo drip irrigation and Himachal Pradesh for kuhls.

relevance.note: Tanka-Rajasthan water-harvesting from NCERT EVS 'Water O Water'; CTET-type

questions.question: When we eat a potato, which part of the plant are we eating?
questions.explanation: A potato is a tuber, which is a swollen underground stem. Its 'eyes' are buds, and buds grow only on stems. A carrot, by contrast, is a root.

relevance.note: Potato is a stem with root trap; CTET EVS plant-part question

questions.question: Houses built on bamboo or wooden stilts, raised above the ground, are most suitable for areas that:
options: Receive heavy rainfall or are prone to floods
Remain snow-covered for most of the year
questions.explanation: Stilt houses, as in Assam, keep living spaces above flood water and damp ground.

relevance.note: Stilt houses for flood/rain areas from NCERT EVS shelter theme

questions.question: In the morning you stand facing the rising sun. Which direction is behind you?
questions.explanation: The sun rises in the east, so if you face east your back is towards the west.

relevance.note: Sun-direction item from NCERT EVS maps chapter; simple but CTET-type

questions.question: As recommended by NCF 2005, EVS in Classes III to V integrates concepts from:
options: Science, social science and environmental education
questions.explanation: NCF 2005 treats EVS at the primary stage as an integrated area drawing on science, social science and environmental education.

relevance.note: NCF integration of science, social science, environmental education is a CTET staple

questions.question: A six-year-old watches juice being poured from a short, wide glass into a tall, narrow glass and then says the tall glass has more juice. According to Piaget, the child is focusing on only one dimension (height). This feature of thinking is called:
questions.explanation: In the pre-operational stage children attend to just one striking feature of a situation (here, height) and ignore others (width). This is centration, which is why they fail conservation tasks. Reversibility is what they lack.

questions.question: A child calls every four-legged animal a "dog". On seeing a cow, her mother explains that it is a different animal, and the child forms a new category "cow". In Piaget's terms, forming the new category is:

questions.question: A teacher gives hints and prompts to a child solving a puzzle and gradually withdraws this help as the child becomes able to solve it alone. This practice, based on Vygotsky's ideas, is called:

questions.question: Riya returns a purse she found in the playground and says, "Good girls are honest, and everyone will think well of me." According to Kohlberg, her reasoning reflects the:

questions.question: A young baby reacts to a toy by excitedly moving its whole body; months later, the same baby simply reaches out with one hand to grasp it. This shows that development proceeds:

questions.question:
Assertion (A): A teacher should find out children's existing ideas about a topic before teaching it.
Reason (R): Children actively construct new knowledge on the basis of what they already know.

Choose the correct option.

Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
questions.explanation: Constructivism holds that learners build new understanding on prior knowledge, including misconceptions. That is exactly why teachers should elicit prior ideas first, so both A and R are true and R explains A.

questions.question: After failing a test, a student says, "I did not prepare enough; next time I will work harder." According to attribution theory, the student attributes failure to:

questions.question: "Metacognition" refers to a learner's:

questions.question:
Read the passage and answer.

"In a small town in Odisha, a retired postman named Harihar noticed that the children of his lane had nothing to read during the summer holidays. He placed an old wooden cupboard outside his house, filled it with forty books from his own shelf and painted a sign above it: 'Take one, bring one back.' At first, the neighbours were doubtful; they expected the books to vanish within a week. Instead, the cupboard slowly grew fuller. Children returned what they borrowed and sometimes added comics, magazines and even handwritten stories of their own. Three years later, the cupboard has become a lending library of more than six hundred books, and older students volunteer to read aloud to the little ones every Sunday evening."

Why did Harihar place the cupboard outside his house?
options: He wanted to sell his old books
The town library had closed down
His neighbours asked him to start a library
The children of his lane had nothing to read during the summer holidays
questions.explanation: The first sentence says he noticed that the children of his lane had nothing to read during the summer holidays.

relevance.note: Reason stated in prose passage; CTET comprehension format

questions.question: According to Noam Chomsky, young children acquire their first language quickly mainly because:

questions.question: Which of the following capital letters has NO line of symmetry?
questions.explanation: A and M have a vertical line of symmetry and H has both vertical and horizontal lines. N has rotational symmetry but no line of symmetry.

relevance.note: Letter symmetry (N none); recurring CTET symmetry item

questions.question: A shop opens at 9:30 a.m. and closes at 7:15 p.m. It closes for 45 minutes at lunch time. For how long is the shop open for business in a day?
questions.explanation: From 9:30 a.m. to 7:15 p.m. is 9 hours 45 minutes. Subtracting the 45-minute lunch break gives 9 hours.

relevance.note: Elapsed time minus lunch break = 9 h; two-step time item with 9h45 trap

questions.question: What comes next in the pattern 3, 6, 11, 18, 27, …?
questions.explanation: The differences are 3, 5, 7, 9, so the next difference is 11. 27 + 11 = 38.

relevance.note: Same odd-difference series as item 041 with new numbers; repetitive but valid

questions.question: A child can state that a rectangle has four right angles and opposite sides equal, but cannot yet see that every square is also a rectangle. According to the van Hiele model, the child is at the level of:
questions.explanation: At the analysis level children describe shapes by their properties but do not yet relate classes of shapes. Seeing that a square is a special rectangle needs informal deduction (level 2).

relevance.note: Properties known but no class inclusion -> analysis; precise van Hiele item

questions.question: Which task is most suitable for assessing a Class III child's understanding of addition, rather than mere recall?
options: Make up a story problem that can be solved by 25 + 17
Add 25 and 17 using the column method
questions.explanation: Creating a word problem requires the child to connect the operation with a real situation, which reveals conceptual understanding. The other tasks test procedure or recall.

relevance.note: Make up a story problem for 25+17 assesses understanding; CTET assessment item

questions.question: A child writes 3/4 + 1/2 = 4/6. The error shows that the child:
options: Does not know basic addition facts
Adds numerators and denominators separately, treating fractions like whole numbers
Cannot find the LCM of 2 and 4
questions.explanation: 3 + 1 = 4 and 4 + 2 = 6: the child applies whole-number addition to the numerator and denominator separately, showing no understanding of a fraction as a single quantity. The addition facts themselves are correct.

relevance.note: 3/4+1/2=4/6 adding numerators/denominators; classic CTET misconception item

questions.question: A Class II child has difficulty with "borrowing" (regrouping) in subtraction such as 42 − 17. The most suitable teaching aid is:
options: Bundles of ten sticks and loose sticks
questions.explanation: Opening a bundle of ten to get ten loose sticks shows concretely why one ten is exchanged for ten ones, which is the idea behind regrouping.

relevance.note: Bundles and loose sticks for regrouping; CTET teaching-aid item

questions.topic: Family & Friends (relationships, animals, plants, work & play)
questions.question: Which bird lays its eggs in the nests of other birds, such as crows, instead of building its own nest?
questions.explanation: The koel does not build a nest; it lays its eggs in a crow's nest and the crow raises the chicks. Weaver birds and tailorbirds are skilled nest-builders.

relevance.note: Koel lays eggs in crow nest — NCERT EVS fact asked in CTET

questions.topic: Family & Friends (relationships, animals, plants, work & play)
questions.question: Seeds of which of the following plants are carried away mainly by the wind?
questions.explanation: Madar seeds have fine silky hairs that let them float on the wind. Coconut is dispersed by water, Xanthium by sticking to animals, and balsam pods burst open.

relevance.note: Madar wind dispersal vs balsam/xanthium/coconut; NCERT seed-dispersal item

questions.question: 'Kuhl', a traditional system of channels that carry water from glacier-fed streams to fields, is found mainly in:
questions.explanation: Kuhls are community-built water channels in the hills of Himachal Pradesh (and Jammu). Tankas and kunds are typical of Rajasthan.

relevance.note: Kuhl in Himachal from NCERT EVS; CTET water-harvesting item

questions.question: Who was the first Indian woman to climb Mount Everest?
questions.explanation: Bachendri Pal reached the summit of Everest in 1984. Santosh Yadav climbed it twice, Arunima Sinha was the first female amputee to do so, and Premlata Agarwal climbed it later.

relevance.note: Bachendri Pal from NCERT Class V 'Up You Go'; CTET-faithful

questions.question: Malaria spreads through the bite of the female:
questions.explanation: The malaria parasite (Plasmodium) is transmitted by the female Anopheles mosquito. Aedes spreads dengue and chikungunya; Culex spreads filariasis.

relevance.note: Anopheles vs Aedes/Culex trap; NCERT EVS malaria content

questions.question: According to NCF 2005, in Classes I and II, environmental concerns are:
options: Taught as a separate subject with its own textbook
Taught as separate science and social science subjects
Integrated with language and mathematics instead of being taught as a separate subject
Kept out of the curriculum until Class III
questions.explanation: NCF 2005 recommends no separate EVS textbook for Classes I–II; the child's environment is used as the context for language and mathematics. EVS becomes a separate integrated subject from Class III.

relevance.note: NCF: EVS integrated with language/maths in Classes I-II; CTET staple

questions.question: Children sort leaves collected from the school garden into groups by shape and size. Which EVS assessment indicator is the teacher mainly observing?
questions.explanation: Grouping objects on the basis of observable features is the indicator "classification" in NCERT's list of EVS assessment indicators.

relevance.note: Leaf sorting -> classification indicator; exact CTET EVS assessment pattern

pyqBlueprint.method: Compiled from the CTET papers of August 2023, January 2024, July 2024 and December 2024 (official question booklets/answer keys as reproduced on coaching sites) and memory-based shift analyses of the February 2026 cycle (no CTET was held in calendar 2025). WebSearch was used for the 2024–2026 analyses (PW, Careers360, Adda247, Prepp); full official papers could not be fetched, so the archetype list also draws on the writer's own knowledge of earlier CTET papers. Patterns are described in our own words; no real question is reproduced. Frequencies are per 30-question section.

archetypes.pattern: Scenario → principle of development (cephalocaudal, proximodistal, general-to-specific, continuity, individual differences, interrelated domains)
"Which statement about development is NOT correct" — stages of childhood/adolescence, development as qualitative and quantitative, lifelong
Nature–nurture: choose the correct statement about the interaction of heredity and environment
Agents of socialisation (family as primary, school/peers/media as secondary) and the teacher's role in socialisation
Child's behaviour → Piagetian stage feature (animism, egocentrism, centration, conservation, object permanence, hypothetico-deductive reasoning)
Piaget's processes: schema, assimilation, accommodation, equilibration identified from an example; distractors swap assimilation/accommodation
Vygotsky: ZPD, scaffolding, more knowledgeable other, private speech, cultural tools — concept from a classroom description
A child's moral reasoning statement → Kohlberg level/stage (punishment-obedience, instrumental, good boy–good girl, law and order, social contract)
Compare/critique the theorists (Piaget vs Vygotsky on language and learning, Gilligan's critique of Kohlberg) — pick the correct statement
Features of child-centred/progressive education and the teacher as facilitator (Dewey, NCF 2005)
Gardner's multiple intelligences from a child's profile; Sternberg's triarchic components; IQ basics
Relationship of language and thought: Vygotsky vs Piaget, Chomsky's LAD, private speech
Gender stereotypes in school practices/textbooks and the teacher's appropriate response; gender as a social construct
Individual differences: sources of diversity and how to address diverse learners (differentiated instruction)
Distinguish assessment of / for / as learning; purpose of CCE and formative vs summative assessment
Assessment tools and NEP 2020 ideas: portfolio, rubrics, open-ended questions, holistic progress card, competency-based assessment

archetypes.topic: Inclusive Education & Children with Special Needs
archetypes.pattern: Symptoms → learning disability/disorder (dyslexia, dysgraphia, dyscalculia, dyspraxia, ADHD, autism)

archetypes.topic: Inclusive Education & Children with Special Needs
archetypes.pattern: Best inclusive practice for a child with a specific disability (visual, hearing, locomotor); RPwD Act 2016 facts; universal design

archetypes.topic: Inclusive Education & Children with Special Needs
archetypes.pattern: Strategies for gifted/creative children and learners from disadvantaged groups (enrichment, divergent tasks, avoiding labelling)
Constructivist view of learning: children's errors and misconceptions as windows into thinking; often in Assertion–Reason format
Motivation: intrinsic vs extrinsic, attribution of success/failure, mastery vs performance goals
Cognition and learning: metacognition, factors affecting learning, emotions and learning, how children think
Factual detail/reason stated in a 150–250-word prose passage; distractors use words from the passage with wrong links
Inference, "NOT supported by the passage" or central idea; trap = option true in general but not stated
Vocabulary in context: synonym/antonym of a word as used in the passage
Grammar item from the passage: part of speech, sentence type, tense/voice, phrase/clause
Literal meaning of a line/stanza of an unseen poem; "which does the poet NOT say"
Poetic device in a quoted line (metaphor, simile, personification, alliteration) or rhyme scheme
Tone/theme of the poem or meaning of a poetic word
Theorists of acquisition (Krashen's input/affective filter, Chomsky's LAD, Vygotsky) and acquisition vs learning; errors as part of learning
Identify a method/approach from a description (whole language, CLT, TPR, direct, grammar-translation, structural)
Best activity to develop listening or speaking at a given class level (role play, storytelling, listening for information)
Name the language sub-skill described (skimming, scanning, intensive vs extensive listening/reading)
Remedial step for a reading/writing difficulty, or choice of authentic/supplementary materials
What a given tool assesses or the best way to assess a skill (cloze, rubric, portfolio, oral tasks)

archetypes.topic: Challenges of Teaching in Multilingual Classrooms
archetypes.pattern: Multilingualism as a resource, use of home language, language across the curriculum
हिंदी गद्यांश से तथ्यात्मक प्रश्न — कारण/विवरण; विकल्पों में गद्यांश के शब्दों का भ्रामक प्रयोग
गद्यांश का आशय, निष्कर्ष, सुझाव या उपयुक्त शीर्षक
गद्यांश के शब्दों पर आधारित व्याकरण/शब्दार्थ — अर्थ, विलोम, समास, कारक, प्रत्यय
संधि-विच्छेद अथवा समास-पहचान (गुण, दीर्घ, यण संधि; तत्पुरुष, द्वंद्व आदि)
पर्यायवाची/विलोम शब्द, "जो पर्यायवाची नहीं है" प्रारूप
बच्चों की भाषायी त्रुटियाँ, घर की भाषा और भाषा-अर्जन के प्रति शिक्षक का दृष्टिकोण
भाषा-अर्जन के सिद्धांत — चॉम्स्की, वाइगोत्स्की, पियाजे, स्किनर के मत की पहचान
व्याकरण-शिक्षण का उपयुक्त तरीका — संदर्भ और प्रयोग के माध्यम से (आगमन विधि), न कि नियम रटवाकर; भाषा-अर्जन बनाम भाषा-अधिगम
पढ़ने-लिखने का विकास — प्रिंट-समृद्ध वातावरण, पठन के उद्देश्य, अर्थग्रहण, बाल-साहित्य
सुनने-बोलने का विकास, कहानी/कविता शिक्षण के उद्देश्य और गतिविधियाँ
भाषा-आकलन के उपकरण और उद्देश्य — सतत आकलन, पोर्टफोलियो, मौखिक आकलन
विशिष्ट भाषायी कठिनाई (ध्वनि-भ्रम, वर्तनी) के लिए उपचारात्मक शिक्षण
बहुभाषिकता को संसाधन मानना, बच्चों की मातृभाषा का कक्षा में उपयोग
Place value vs face value, number names in Indian system (lakh/thousand), writing numerals with zeros; traps from misplaced zeros
One-step/two-step word problem on the four operations (sharing, grouping, buses/boxes needed); trap = ignoring the remainder or wrong operation
Compare/order or add fractions and decimals; distractors from adding numerators and denominators or misreading decimals
Properties of 2-D/3-D shapes: faces–edges–vertices, lines of symmetry of letters/figures, nets, angles in shapes
Unit conversion and elapsed-time/calendar/money computation (a.m.–p.m. intervals, kg–g, km–m); trap = treating time as decimal
Perimeter/area of rectangle or square in a context (fencing rounds, tiling, cost); trap = mixing area with perimeter
Next term of a number/shape pattern with growing differences, or reading a pictograph/bar graph with a scale (one symbol = k units)
van Hiele level / nature of maths (abstract, logical, patterns) identified from a child's geometric reasoning or a teacher statement

archetypes.pattern: NCF 2005 goal of school maths (mathematisation of thinking) and the role of language/maths-talk in learning maths
Linking classroom maths to everyday life (shopping, measuring at home, local crafts) — choose the best community-based practice

A child's written error (subtraction regrouping, fraction addition, place value) — identify the underlying misconception
Choose the teaching aid or remedial strategy (bundles of sticks, Dienes blocks, abacus, concrete–pictorial–abstract) for a diagnosed difficulty

Why NCERT EVS uses narratives, themes, open questions and discussion rather than definitions
Identify the NCERT EVS assessment indicator (observation & recording, classification, questioning, concern for justice & equality, cooperation) from a classroom scenario
Choose the most appropriate learning resource (local resource persons, real objects, surroundings) for an EVS theme
